Title: GTerminal
ShortDescription: A lightweight terminal for Windows with tmux-style session persistence: closing a tab, closing the window, or even rebooting doesn't lose your terminals.
Description:
GTerminal is a lightweight terminal for Windows with one defining feature: your sessions don't die. Close a tab, close the window, or reboot the machine — your terminals come back, scrollback and working directory intact.

SESSIONS THAT SURVIVE
A background daemon owns every shell, and the window is just a thin client. Close the window and everything keeps running; reopen and you're back where you were. Sessions are checkpointed every few seconds, so even after a reboot they're restored cold: a fresh shell in the saved directory with the old scrollback replayed behind a divider. If Claude Code was running in a session, resuming the conversation is a single Enter away.

THE "OOPS" GRACE WINDOW
Killing a session doesn't actually kill it — the tab closes but the process keeps running for five minutes, with a live countdown in the sidebar. One click restores it and cancels the kill entirely. An accidental "exit" is just as recoverable. Kill something twice to skip the grace.

TABS THAT WORK LIKE YOU DO
Browser-style tabs that shrink as they multiply, colored collapsible tab groups, custom names that stick, and park-a-tab-as-a-pill for things you want out of the way. Tab icons show what's running inside (Claude Code, python, cargo, docker, and more). Groups, names, and layout persist across restarts and reboots. Drag tabs to reorder, pin up to three custom badges on any session, and size tabs your way: Ctrl+scroll over the tab bar for a global width, or drag a single tab's edge to give just that tab its own. A dotted grip beside the window controls means there is always a spot to drag the window by, even with a packed strip.

EVERY SESSION, TRANSCRIBED
Full transcripts of every session are kept on disk (14 days by default, configurable) behind a built-in history page: search across everything you have run, reopen any transcript, and read it with its original colors.

AUTOCOMPLETE THAT KNOWS YOUR HABITS
A per-directory predictor learns from the commands you actually type and suggests them back through PSReadLine — inline ghost text or a list, from your habits alone or blended with shell history, or off entirely. It knows that what you run in one project folder is not what you run in another.

TEMPLATES AND DEFAULTS
Set a default working directory for new tabs, and define session templates — shell, folder, and title presets one right-click away on the new-tab button.

FORTY-FIVE COMPLETE THEMES
From clean classics (Nord, Gruvbox, Solarized, Catppuccin) to full scene themes with generated backdrop art: retro amber CRT, Matrix rain, synthwave sunset, deep space with real NASA imagery, and more. Each theme is a whole look — its own font, line spacing, cursor personality, and backdrop, individually overridable — and the entire chrome recolors with the terminal. Every theme is contrast-audited for readability. Or build your own: pick any built-in as a base and override its background, text, and accent colors with color pickers, right from Settings.

SMART TITLES, YOUR RULES
Right-click a tab for title suggestions computed locally from what's on screen — running program, last command, directory. Optionally point it at your own AI endpoint (Anthropic- or OpenAI-compatible, including local gateways like Ollama) for AI-suggested titles; this is off by default and nothing is ever called unless you configure it.

ZEN MODE
F11 strips away everything but the terminal in true full screen, leaving a small draggable exit pill that pings like sonar for a few seconds so you never lose it.

CLIPBOARD, CONSIDERED
The right-click menu shows what you are about to paste before you paste it, keeps your last three clipboard entries a click away with a full history viewer, and returns focus to the terminal after every paste.

YOUR SHELLS
PowerShell 7, Windows PowerShell, and Command Prompt. Set a default, open one-off tabs in any shell, and each session remembers its shell across restarts — with working-directory tracking in all of them.

FAST AND LIGHT
Built on Tauri (WebView2) and xterm.js with the WebGL renderer — far lighter than an Electron equivalent, with typing latency regression-tested on every build. Source available at github.com/guscatalano/GTerminal.
Features: Sessions survive closed tabs, closed windows, and reboots — scrollback and working directory restored
Background daemon keeps shells alive; the window is just a thin client you can close anytime
"Oops" grace window: killed sessions stay restorable for five minutes with a live countdown
Colored, collapsible tab groups and custom tab names that persist across reboots
Tab icons show what's running inside (Claude Code, python, cargo, docker, ...)
45 complete themes with backdrop art, each with its own font, spacing, and cursor personality
Custom themes: build your own from any built-in base with background, text, and accent pickers
Searchable history: full transcripts of past sessions, replayed with their original colors
Autocomplete that learns per directory from your own commands (inline ghost text or list)
Default working directory plus session templates: shell, folder, and title presets
Resizable tabs: global width on Ctrl+scroll, or drag one tab's edge to size it alone
Zen full-screen mode (F11) with a draggable exit pill
Clipboard paste preview and three-entry clipboard history in the right-click menu
Local tab-title suggestions, plus optional AI titles via your own endpoint (off by default)
PowerShell 7, Windows PowerShell, and Command Prompt with per-session shell memory
Lightweight Tauri + xterm.js WebGL stack — far lighter than Electron
Typing latency regression-tested: p50 echo latency around 1-2 ms
ReleaseNotes: 0.2.7 — Two new themes: Pip-Boy, a phosphor-green console screen complete with a thumbs-up mascot, radiation gauge, radio graph, and CRT scanlines; and NieR, the beige menu look with drop-shadowed UI bars and dithered paper. Plus custom themes: build your own from any built-in base and override its background, text, and accent colors with color pickers in Settings. Previous release added workspaces (launch a preconfigured set of sessions from one desktop shortcut) and fixed the white flash on window open.
